subject: POC kickoff confirmation — scope, metrics, and access checklist (Novapulse)
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
To: Ava Simmons <ava.simmons@novapulse.ai>, Ethan Lyle <ethan.lyle@novapulse.ai>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 09 Mar 2027 15:04:00 -0700
Subject: POC kickoff confirmation — scope, metrics, and access checklist (Novapulse)

Thanks again for the call today — good to meet the Novapulse team. I wanted to capture the outcomes and next steps so everyone has a single reference. Please reply with any corrections or missing owners.

Key pain points we heard
- Latency on batch enrichment calls (p95 ~ 600-800ms) causing downstream queueing
- Model hallucination on rare product codes impacting catalog accuracy (~3% error in current V1)
- Cost sensitivity for high-volume nightly jobs — target is to reduce token cost by 40% vs current setup

Proposed POC scope (what Redwood will demonstrate)
1) Integration: ingest sample nightly batch (10k records) -> run generation + reranking pipeline using our streaming endpoint
2) Quality: run a 1k prompt eval set (provided by Novapulse) to measure hallucination/accuracy improvements
3) Performance: measure p50/p95 token latency under a representative concurrency profile (10 concurrent workers)
4) Cost: provide baseline vs optimized config (batching + quantization) and estimate per-1M-token cost

Success metrics (mutually agreed)
- p95 end-to-end token latency <= 350ms for production-like requests
- Hallucination rate <= 1% on the 1k prompt eval set (we'll run before/after)
- Unit cost <= 60% of current per-token spend for the nightly job

Owners and roles
- Novapulse product: Ava Simmons (PO) — primary decision maker for acceptance
- Novapulse infra: Ethan Lyle — will own sandbox network and IAM access
- Redwood: Jonas Weber — engagement lead / outcomes and timeline
- Redwood: Karthik Iyer — ML engineer (model config & evals)
- Redwood: Marissa Cole — integration & SRE liaison

Timeline (tentative)
- Week 0 (this week): exchange sample data & eval prompts; provide access constraints
- Week 1: Redwood provision sandbox endpoint + run initial smoke tests
- Week 2: Iteration on model config & run 1k eval suite
- Week 3: Performance run & cost analysis; joint readout and acceptance decision

Access required from Novapulse (ask to provide by EOD Thu)
- S3 (or equivalent) link to sample nightly batch (10k records) with schema notes
- Short list (CSV) of 1k prompt variants and expected correctness labels
- IP allowlist for sandbox endpoint OR temporary VPN/Tunnel details
- Contact for your security reviewer if SOC 2 docs/answers needed

Attachments: I attached a kickoff mutual-action-plan (MAP) and an access checklist for the sandbox.

Please hit reply to confirm the timeline and the list of missing items. If the timeline looks tight on your side, tell us which week you'd prefer to start.

Thanks,
Jonas Weber
Senior Solutions Lead | Redwood Inference
jonas.weber@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0142

From: Ava Simmons <ava.simmons@novapulse.ai>

Cc: Ethan Lyle <ethan.lyle@novapulse.ai>
Date: Wed, 10 Mar 2027 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: POC kickoff confirmation — scope, metrics, and access checklist (Novapulse)

Thanks Jonas — this is a great summary. Confirming a few adjustments from our side so we’re aligned:

1) Scope change: for the quality eval, we want to include an additional "edge cases" subset (~150 records) that contains historical problematic SKUs. Can you run separate results for edge vs core?
2) Timeline: Week 1 provisioning is tight for our infra team. Can we shift start by one week (provision in Week 2, full runs Weeks 3-4)? Still OK to do readout in Week 5.
3) Access: Ethan will send a presigned S3 link to the sample batch and the 1k prompt CSV by Thursday EOD. For IP allowlisting we prefer a CIDR block — Ethan, I’ll loop you below.

Additional people to include:
- Sameer Patel (secops@novapulse.ai) — security reviewer for SOC 2/Q&A (please include for any compliance artifacts)

Quadruple-checking acceptance criteria: we agree to the p95 and hallucination targets, but for cost the acceptance threshold is softer — an estimate and plan to get to <=60% is acceptable for signoff.

Quoted for context:
> Success metrics (mutually agreed)
> - p95 end-to-end token latency <= 350ms for production-like requests
> - Hallucination rate <= 1% on the 1k prompt eval set (we'll run before/after)
> - Unit cost <= 60% of current per-token spend for the nightly job

I'll reply with the S3 link and Sameer's contact in the next mail. Looking forward to kicking off.

Best,
Ava Simmons
Head of Product | Novapulse
ava.simmons@novapulse.ai
